analysis.evidence: The two direct objects, אֶת לוֹט and וְאֶת רְכֻשׁוֹ, identify whom and what the raiders seized. They took Lot captive along with his possessions and then departed (וַיֵּלֵכוּ).
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine plural Qal wayyiqtol. The subject is the raiding party.
analysis.sense: capture a person and seize property as spoil

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְחוּ אֶת לוֹט, “they took Lot,” אֶת marks the proper name לוֹט as the direct object of וַיִּקְחוּ. The parallel וְאֶת רְכֻשׁוֹ marks “his possessions” as the second object of the same verb.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The genealogy lists Abram and Haran among Terah’s sons and names Lot as Haran’s son.
וְלוֹט עִמּוֹ names Lot as a companion of Abram on the journey from Egypt.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Lot was the son of Haran, Abram’s brother. He accompanied Abram from Egypt toward the Negeb. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט. The derivation of the name is uncertain.
draft.definition: Lot, son of Haran and nephew of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Haran as Lot’s father. Genesis 13:1 names Lot as Abram’s companion on the journey from Egypt.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks לוֹט as a direct object of וַיִּקְחוּ (“they took”). בֶּן אֲחִי אַבְרָם (“son of Abram’s brother”) identifies Lot as Abram’s nephew.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Gen 14:12 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense of word 0.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, here a noun made definite by its possessive suffix.
draft.evidence: Gen 14:12 repeats the object marker before רְכֻשׁוֹ, coordinating Lot’s possessions with Lot as the things and person taken.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת לוֹט וְאֶת רְכֻשׁוֹ, the repeated אֶת marks both Lot and his possessions as objects of “they took.” The possessive suffix on רְכֻשׁוֹ makes the second object definite.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” is prefixed to אֶת, the unsuffixed direct-object marker.
analysis.sense: Marks רְכֻשׁוֹ, “his possessions,” as the second definite direct object of וַיִּקְחוּ, “they took.”

draft.change: Add the root רכש and its noun רְכוּשׁ for acquired possessions. The source’s personal-name gloss does not fit this occurrence.
draft.definition: Property or goods that someone owns, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:5 pairs רְכוּשָׁם, “their possessions,” with רָכָשׁוּ, “they had acquired.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְחוּ אֶת לוֹט וְאֶת רְכֻשׁוֹ, the repeated object marker אֶת identifies both Lot and his possessions as objects of “they took.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Lot.

analysis.evidence: בֶּן אֲחִי אַבְרָם identifies Lot as the son of Abram’s brother. בֶּן expresses Lot’s relationship to his father, and the full phrase identifies him as Abram’s nephew.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בֶּן אֲחִי אַבְרָם identifies Lot as the son of Abram’s brother. אֲחִי names the relationship of Lot’s father to Abram.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state. The following name אַבְרָם supplies the possessor.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: The phrase בֶּן אֲחִי אַבְרָם identifies Lot as the son of Abram’s brother. אַבְרָם names Lot’s uncle and completes the construct chain.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The plural subject carries over from וַיִּקְחוּ, “they took.” After taking Lot and his possessions, the captors depart.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol. The י־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural.

analysis.evidence: In וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב בִּסְדֹם, “and he was living in Sodom,” הוּא refers back to Lot and serves as the subject of the masculine singular participle יֹשֵׁב.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a background clause. הוּא is an independent third-person masculine singular pronoun.

analysis.evidence: וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב בִּסְדֹם gives the background to Lot’s capture. The participle describes his ongoing residence, and בִּסְדֹם identifies Sodom as the place where he was living.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, agreeing with הוּא, which refers to Lot.
analysis.sense: to dwell habitually in a place

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:12 as evidence for the existing sodom sense.
draft.definition: Sodom, the city where Lot lived.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:12 identifies Sodom as Lot’s place of residence with יֹשֵׁב בִּסְדֹם.

analysis.evidence: וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב בִּסְדֹם means “and he was living in Sodom.” The prepositional phrase identifies where Lot lived.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ takes the form בִּ before the initial sheva of the place name סְדֹם.
